This is a topic that can and does apply to adults as well, but I'm going to put this in the context of raising our kids. As a parent, it is our responsibility to make sure that our kids stay safe, including around guns. Being ignorant of guns is not safe. If you don't own a gun and don't have friends who own guns, you probably still live near a firing range that will allow you to shoot their guns at their range for a fee. Most also offer gun safety and shooting classes. My point is: there is no good excuse to not learn, practice, and exercise gun safety and teach it to your children.

Everyone has heard of the story of Little Johnny who was playing at a friend's house, found the Dad's gun, started foolishly playing around with it, and ended up shooting the other kid. The lesson ends up being "so, kid, if you see a gun at your friend's house, don't touch it, and go get help". That message is all fine and dandy until you hear of the story of Little Johnny playing at his friend's house, finding the friend's Dad's gun, he then leaves the room to go get help, and his friend ends up shooting himself with the gun in Johnny's absence. The lesson here is "kid, if you see a gun at your friend's house, unload the gun, and then go find an adult". Obviously, a really small kid may not have the strength to disarm a heavy firearm; you can't do much there except tell him to bring his friend along with him to find that adult. However, in general, everyone will benefit if a kid knows what he's doing around guns, compared to if he is completely ignorant.

Basic NRA gun safety rules that should be taught to every child:

  • Always keep the gun pointed in a safe direction. Older kids could understand this wording a little better too: do not point the gun at anything that you aren't willing to completely destroy.

  • Always keep your finger off of the trigger until you are ready to shoot. Keep that finger laying straight across that trigger guard.

  • Always keep the gun unloaded until ready to use.

Additional lesson: teach your kid how to safely unload guns. If they come across a gun that is laying around loaded, then they will know how to make the situation safe. The above rules apply (keep the gun pointed away in a safe direction, finger off the trigger), and gun models are all a little different, but if kids have the basics down, they will be able to unload the rounds and/or magazine.
